name: Ugali
description: Boiled maize meal, the base of most Kenyan meals. High in starch, so keep the portion small.

name: Sukuma Wiki
description: Collard greens stewed with tomato and onion. Very low carbohydrate and very filling.

name: Chapati
description: Wheat flatbread rolled with ghee. Filling, but it spikes blood sugar quickly.

name: Matoke
description: Green plantain stewed with tomato and onion, a Luhya staple.

name: Githeri
description: Maize and beans cooked together. Beans bring the protein and slow the sugar rise.

name: Mandazi
description: Swollen fried dough, best with tea. A classic Kenyan breakfast.

name: Uji
description: Fermented millet drink, warm and sour. Gentle on the stomach and cheap.

name: Omelette with Spinach
description: Two eggs beaten with spinach and tomato. Almost no carbohydrate.

name: Whole Wheat Bread with Avocado
description: Two slices of wholemeal bread with half an avocado. Low GI and good for fibre.

name: Oats, Banana and Peanut Butter
description: Slow-release oats with a sliced banana and a spoon of peanut butter.

name: Boiled Egg with Black Tea
description: One boiled egg and a cup of unsweetened black tea. The cheapest breakfast in Kenya.

name: Mandazi and Chai
description: Two mandazi with a cup of milk tea. Comforting, but high in refined starch.

name: White Rice
description: One cup of steamed white rice. Low fibre, so it raises blood sugar quickly.

name: Nyama Choma
description: Roasted beef, the pride of Kenyan carnivores. No carbohydrate at all.

name: Fried Tilapia
description: Whole tilapia fried in a little oil. Omega-3 and zero carbohydrate.

name: Chicken Stew (Mchuzi wa Kuku)
description: Chicken simmered in tomato and onion with vegetables.

name: Beef Stew (Mchuzi wa Nyama)
description: Beef slow-cooked in tomato gravy with green pepper.

name: Green Beans
description: Boiled green beans. Low GI and a decent amount of fibre.

name: Black-eyed Peas (Ndama)
description: Boiled ndama beans. Cheap protein with a very low glycemic index.

name: Cowpeas (Nduma)
description: Boiled nduma, seasoned with tomato and onion.

name: Boiled Lentils
description: Lentils cooked soft with a little oil and salt. One of the lowest GI staples.

name: Kidney Beans
description: Boiled red kidney beans, a common side in Swahili cooking.

name: Fish Stew (Mchuzi wa Samaki)
description: Fish pieces in a tomato and onion sauce, the heart of a Nyanza weeknight.

name: Kachumbari
description: Tomato, cucumber and onion salad with salt and oil. Almost free of carbohydrate.

name: Stir-fried Cabbage
description: Shredded cabbage fried with onion and tomato.

name: Cooked Spinach
description: Spinach boiled with onion. Very low GI and full of iron.

name: Collard Greens with Tomato
description: Sukuma wiki cooked down with ripe tomato and onion.

name: Raw Carrots
description: A cup of raw carrot sticks. Sweet, crunchy and low GI.

name: Okra with Tomato (Ochodo)
description: Okra stewed with tomato, onion and a little groundnut.

name: Butternut Squash Stew (Mukanga)
description: Sweet potato or butternut simmered with greens and onions.

name: Sukuma Wiki with Egg
description: Collard greens with a fried egg on top. Protein without the starch.

name: Lentil Soup
description: Lentil soup with carrot, celery and kale. Warming and low GI.

name: Vegetable Soup
description: Light soup made from whatever is in the market that morning.

name: Pilau (Chicken and Rice)
description: Spiced rice with chicken. Delicious, but the white rice pushes the GI up.

name: Muthamaki
description: Black-eyed pea stew with tomato, onion and coconut milk.

name: Beef Broth with Rice
description: Clear beef broth served with a portion of rice.

name: Groundnuts
description: A small bowl of roasted groundnuts. Cheap fat and protein that curbs snacking.

name: Samosa
description: One meat or potato samosa from the roadside. Crispy, salty and high in starch.

name: Banana
description: One medium ripe banana. Good value, but ripeness pushes the GI up.

name: Apple
description: One medium apple. Low GI and high in fibre.

name: Boiled Cassava (Muhogo)
description: Boiled cassava from the coast. Cheap and filling, but very high in starch.

name: Boiled Irish Potato
description: One boiled potato. Filling and cheap, but one of the highest GI staples.
